task: EPMCDME-14217 part 1 — capture the MCP initialize-handshake `instructions` string and expose it additively as a top-level `instructions` key on tools/list bridge responses.

key_reasoning.reason: Four production components: a new client/instructions.py value object plus sanitizer, ManagedClient's lifecycle task, the single-usage executor's three transport bodies, and the server route handler. The change is not local to one call site — it retypes the lifecycle handshake channel (ready_future) that all three transports share, and alters the get_or_create_client return contract. Base M for a thin additive feature, bumped to L because it touches the shared client lifecycle contract.

No precedent in the codebase for carrying handshake-time data out of the lifecycle task, and the retyping had a silent failure mode: a missed declaration site or transport body yields a 30-second hang rather than a type error. The relayed text is third-party and lands in a downstream LLM system prompt, so instructions.py became a trust boundary needing a size cap and control-character strip — findings the code review surfaced rather than the plan. Offsetting factors: the change is additive, backward compatible and trivially reversible, and the repository has no CI, so all eight quality gates were run by hand.

14 real source files touched (6 new), spanning src/mcp_connect/client/, src/mcp_connect/server/, tests/, tests/integration/, plus README.md, .env.example and .ai-run/guides/quality-gates.md. Falls in the 11-15 modified / 4-6 new band. Note the profile is test-heavy: production code is roughly 230 lines across 4 files, while 5 of the 6 new files are tests. The 22-file diffstat figure is not used — 11 of those files and ~3900 lines are SDLC run artifacts under docs/superpowers/tasks/.

red_flags_applied: Technical Risk bumped from M to L: security-sensitive trust boundary — server-supplied text is relayed into a downstream LLM prompt, requiring a size cap and control-character sanitization.

Component Scope bumped from M to L: touches a core shared contract — ready_future retyped from Future[ClientSession] to Future[SessionHandshake] across six declaration sites and three transport bodies, plus the get_or_create_client return shape.
notes: No initial complexity-assessment.json exists for comparison; this run used sdlc-light, which scores only at the end. The total of 21 sits at the very bottom of the L band, one point from M. Kept at L per the borderline rule: leaning lower requires Technical Risk of M or below with existing patterns covering more than half the implementation, and neither held — there was no existing pattern for handshake capture. Effort drivers not visible in the diff: a code-review round producing four findings (missing size cap and control-character strip, overwrite of a server-supplied key, unguarded pydantic setattr that could return 500, coverage gaps) and a fifth in the check round (docs contradicting the new behaviour); a cross-repo contract with a paired codemie backend MR; and manual execution of all quality gates because the repository has no CI. Affected Layers stayed at M (client/transport, API/server route, config-and-docs) — the cross-repo consumer is part 2 and not in this diff, though the /bridge response schema is a contract deployed clients depend on.
